articles.title: NFL world reacts to Fred Warner's fines from Monday's game vs Commanders
articles.summary: Social media reacts to 49ers LB Fred Warner's hefty fines from Monday's game against the Commanders.
articles.body:
On Saturday, the NFL announced it fined San Francisco 49ers star linebacker Fred Warner $65,673 for two hits on Washington Commanders tight end Chig Okonkwo in Monday night's 23-17 Niners win.

Officials initially ruled one play a penalty on the field, but then incorrectly picked it up. Washington fans were irate during Monday's game, as it was the latest in a recent series of questionable calls against the Commanders. San Francisco safety Malik Mustapha got away with an illegal hit against Washington wide receiver Stefon Diggs on the Commanders' first drive. It was on third down, and Washington had to settle for a field goal.

The fines against Warner were the NFL's admission that its officials got it wrong—at least twice. That doesn't mean it would have changed the result of the game. Washington had its chances, including scoring on a go-ahead fourth-quarter touchdown that was wiped out by an unnecessary facemask penalty on left guard Chris Paul—it was a correct call.

Still, the NFL world reacted to Warner's illegal hits and subsequent fines from Monday's game.

articles.title: Browns extend defensive player with $30 million deal overnight
articles.summary: Talented run defender gets two more years.
articles.body:
The defensive tackle spot this year has been a roller coaster with various players missing time. But Maliek Collins has been a steady hand in regards to his run defense.

On Saturday, the Browns rewarded his efforts by inking him to a two-year contract extension worth $30 million.

The defensive tackle group started the season as one of the bright spots on this year's defense, but then different members began to get injured , such as Mason Graham and Mike Hall. This forced other players to step up and step in, as Collins kept showing up.

Collins has played and started all six games on the schedule this season. He has 16 total tackles, five of which are for a loss. He also has 3.5 sacks, which is uncommon for a defensive tackle to be able to place that much pressure in the opposing backfield on passing downs.

Other stats include 8 QB hits, 8 pressures, 4 knockdowns, and just 2 missed tackles.

The deal is for another two years with $23 million guaranteed. This was the final year of his two-year contract he signed at the beginning of last season. In 2025, Collins had 6.5 sacks, 25 QB hits, and 15 pressures, among other stats, in a season in which he suffered a season-ending quad injury that placed him on IR.

It seems that Collins has been the only defensive tackle who hasn't seen the doctor on a regular basis. Graham began the season with four sacks and then had an ankle sprain plus a left MCL sprain in the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. He has been out since, but is expected to return against the Tennessee Titans. Hall has only played in four games with zero starts. He injured his right ankle in the Steelers game as well. The injury seems to be persistent, and his return is questionable. Backup Adin Huntington has filled the void while the injured players have missed time.

Collins came to the Browns beginning in 2025 after stints with the San Francisco 49ers, Houston Texans, Las Vegas Raiders, and the Dallas Cowboys. He was selected in Round 3 of the 2016 NFL Draft by Dallas.

articles.title: Will Saquon Barkley play in Week 7? Injury update, start or sit advice for Eagles RB
articles.summary: Here's what we know about Saquon Barkley's chances of suiting up on Monday night.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have a chance to get running back Saquon Barkley back for the Week 7 game against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night.

The Eagles have been without their star running back for each of the past two weeks after Barkley came down with a hamstring injury that forced his early exit in Week 4.

This week, Barkley returned to practice and logged two limited and one full session during the week before drawing the questionable tag for Monday.

Here's what we know about Barkley's status for Week 7.

Despite the questionable tag, Barkley is expected to play in Week 7 on Monday night, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

"DeVonta Smith is out, while Saquon Barkley is questionable but expected to play," Rapoport said on Saturday afternoon.

This is not at all surprising considering Barkley's practice participation during the week.

We would have been more skeptical if Barkley only practiced on a limited basis, but the full practice on Saturday shows he's all but confirmed to go.

The Eagles are in a bad way offensively right now after losing Jalen Hurts for the season , which has an impact on the entire offense.

Not only do the Eagles have to start Tanner McKee, who is a significant downgrade from Hurts as a passer, but they are also without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks , which should make moving the football even more difficult.

That, in turn, could leave Barkley with less scoring opportunities. It could also, however, force the Eagles to lean more on him on the ground and through the air.

There is legitimate concern for the Eagles' offense, but this is a juicy matchup against a Cowboys defense that has been a sieve this season.

The Cowboys are permitting the eighth-most fantasy points per game to backs this season, according to CBS Sports , and the most rushing yards per game.

Dallas also hasn't been able to stop a nosebleed through the air, with the Cowboys' defense giving up the 10th-most passing yards per contest, so even McKee and what's left of Philly's pass-catchers could eat.

This might be the best spot for Barkley to produce for the rest of the season. He's an easy lineup decision this week, despite the issues on the Eagles' offense.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Brian Thomas Jr., Jerry Jeudy, Khalil Mack, Chop Robinson and More
articles.summary: With the NFL's 2026 trade deadline a little more than two weeks away, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter provided updates on notable veterans who could be on the move.
articles.body:
With the NFL's 2026 trade deadline a little more than two weeks away, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter provided updates on notable veterans who could be on the move.

On Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., the two insiders reported the team "has shown no signs of engaging in trade talks." Interested suitors could press the issue, however, as the deadline gets closer.

It appears to be the same situation with the Cleveland Browns' Jerry Jeudy.

"The Browns aren't shopping Jeudy at all, and the price is high," per Rapoport and Schefter. "It would take a premium deal to get Cleveland to move on — even if general manager Andrew Berry is open to discussing any deal. But as of right now, a Jeudy deal seems unlikely."

Three teams on the outside of the playoff picture sound similarly resolute on some edge defenders who are garnering trade interest.

The 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers "have given no indication that they are willing to make any trades at this time," and that includes one involving impending free agent Khalil Mack, according to Rapoport and Schefter

The Miami Dolphins could probably net a nice asset or two for Chop Robinson, but the 2024 first-round pick is someone they can keep building around beyond this season.

The Arizona Cardinals, meanwhile, at least "could be willing to listen to meaningful offers" for Josh Sweat, per Sunday's report. Rapoport and Schefter cited the Dallas Cowboys as one potential landing spot for the 2021 Pro Bowler.

Midseason trades used to be rare in the NFL, but those days are long gone. Along the same lines, general managers aren't afraid to cut bait on younger players who aren't fulfilling their potential.

Two top-10 picks from the 2024 NFL draft are already on new teams: wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and quarterback J.J. McCarthy.

Like his fellow draftee, Thomas is in the midst of a tough season. He has caught nine passes for 105 yards and a touchdown. The 2024 Pro Bowler has gone two straight games without a reception.

A 2027 second-round pick was the best asset the Cardinals got back for Harrison, and that may have helped to inform teams what it could take to get Thomas out of Jacksonville.

He'd seemingly benefit from a change of scenery with Parker Washington emerging as the No. 1 option in the passing game.

Mack's exit from Los Angeles might only be a matter of time because it's making increasingly less sense to hold onto him.

The Chargers are long shots for the playoffs, and the nine-time Pro Bowler is on an expiring contract. Even if the franchise doesn't want to blow it up and rebuild, Mack likely doesn't have much of a long-term future in Southern California.

Flipping him for any sort of draft compensation is a better value play than simply letting him walk as a free agent in the offseason.

articles.title: 'Manchild' Braelon Allen Hyped by Derrick Henry amid Jets RB Breece Hall's Injury Recovery
articles.summary: New York Jets running back Braelon Allen merited high praise from one of the best at the position.
articles.body:
New York Jets running back Braelon Allen merited high praise from one of the best at the position.

The Baltimore Ravens' Derrick Henry told Rich Cimini of ESPN he has tried to impart some wisdom to Allen and has been impressed by his work while filling in for an injured Breece Hall.

"Don't give no credit to me; he's his own man," Henry said. "I'm trying to be someone who can help him out in any way I can give advice.

"But, yeah, he's just a big, physical kid. I call him 'Manchild,' and I was able to catch a little bit of clips from the games he's played. He's doing a heck of a job being in that starting role and always knew he'd be ready for it, so I'm happy for him."

According to Cimini, the friendship between Allen and Henry began when the former was a freshman at Wisconsin. They have since trained together in the offseason, and the more experienced Henry is willing to provide any helpful advice when necessary.

"In my shoes, he's really the best you can get in terms of a guy, a connection, someone that can mentor and guide me through the process of my career," Allen said of the five-time Pro Bowler. "He's been great. I try to get every little nugget that I can about what he does. He doesn't slow down. I want to have a long career, too, so I try to soak up as much as possible."

With Allen getting featured like never before thanks to Hall's absence, all of the tutelage might be paying off.

The 2024 fourth-round pick has run for 253 yards and one touchdown over New York's last three games. He eclipsed the century mark for the first time in a 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns.

Henry is a one-of-a-kind back in terms of his frame and speed. But the 6'1", 235-pound Allen did draw some comparisons to the Ravens star when he was coming out of college.

While he has a long way to go to reach Henry's status, Allen is at least making a strong case for himself to remain a No. 1 option moving forward.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers throws 540th career touchdown, passing Peyton Manning on all-time list
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers now sits third all-time in passing touchdowns.
articles.body:
When Aaron Rodgers retires from the NFL, he'll go down as one of the best quarterbacks of his era. While that's been the case for years, Rodgers found a way to remind fans of his place in NFL history in Week 7.

With his second-quarter touchdown pass to Darnell Washington, Rodgers passed Indianapolis Colts legend Peyton Manning for third place on the all-time passing touchdowns list.

Rodgers managed the achievement on a jump ball to Washington, who bullied a defender and somehow held onto the ball as he was shoved out of bounds.

The score put the Pittsburgh Steelers up 10-3 with roughly five minutes to play before halftime.

With the touchdown, Rodgers now has 540 passing scores in his career. That figure puts Rodgers behind only Drew Brees and Tom Brady.

It was only a matter of time before Rodgers passed Manning on the all-time list. The 42-year-old Rodgers entered the 2026 season just 12 touchdowns shy of tying Manning. He reached that figure in only six games, and entered Week 7 just a score away from breaking the tie.

It's unlikely Rodgers moves any higher on the all-time passing touchdowns list. Following his second-quarter touchdown, Rodgers sat 31 passing touchdowns behind Brees for second.

While it's tough to fully count out a player of Rodgers' caliber, adding 31 more touchdowns in the remaining 10 regular-season games is a massive ask of any player, let alone one in his 22nd NFL season.

If Rodgers really wanted to pass Brees, the Steelers' quarterback would likely have to play another season. That doesn't seem likely after Rodgers stated 2026 would be his final year in the NFL.

articles.title: $900 million to $2.6 billion: Patrick Mahomes’ Alpine F1 investment draws attention as team valuation surges nearly 189%
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has built a reputation for winning on the football field, but his business interests are taking him into another high-profile arena.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has built a reputation for winning on the football field, but his business interests are taking him into another high-profile arena. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback joined an investor group backing Alpine's Formula 1 team in 2023, entering a sport that has attracted growing interest from celebrities, athletes and major investors. Since that deal, Alpine's estimated value has climbed from around $900 million to approximately $2.6 billion, marking a remarkable increase of nearly 189%. The rise highlights Formula 1's growing commercial appeal and puts Mahomes' investment among the more interesting chapters of his expanding business portfolio.Patrick Mahomes joins Alpine F1's investor groupMahomes entered Formula 1 ownership in October 2023 alongside Chiefs teammate Travis Kelce. Both joined an investor group led by Otro Capital, which had partnered with RedBird Capital Partners and Maximum Effort Investments, the firm associated with actor Ryan Reynolds.The group had acquired a 24% stake in Alpine Racing Ltd for €200 million earlier that year. Renault Group, Alpine's parent company, announced the transaction in June 2023 and said the investment valued the racing business at approximately $900 million. The deal closed in December.The investment brought together people from different corners of sport and entertainment. Alongside Mahomes and Kelce, the wider group included golfer Rory McIlroy, boxer Anthony Joshua and footballers Trent Alexander-Arnold and Juan Mata.For Mahomes, the opportunity offered a route into a global sport with a growing audience in the United States. Formula 1 has expanded its reach through new races, streaming coverage and popular entertainment content. Its international calendar also gives investors opportunities to connect with fans and commercial partners across multiple markets.The move fits a broader pattern among professional athletes. Instead of relying solely on playing contracts and endorsement deals, some are investing in sports teams and businesses that could gain value over time.However, Mahomes' personal investment amount has not been publicly disclosed. The €200 million figure represents the consortium's purchase of the entire 24% stake, not Mahomes' individual contribution.Alpine F1 valuation rises from $900 million to $2.6 billionThe biggest financial development is the rise in Alpine's estimated value since the 2023 investment.At the time of the original deal, Alpine Racing Ltd was valued at roughly $900 million. By August 2026, an estimate cited by F1Salaries placed the team's value at $2.6 billion, putting it among the more valuable operations on the Formula 1 grid.The difference is substantial.Valuation measureReported estimateAlpine's value in 2023$900 millionEstimated value in 2026$2.6 billionIncrease in estimated value$1.7 billionPercentage increaseApproximately 189%These figures indicate that Alpine's estimated value has nearly tripled in about three years. The increase is approximately $1.7 billion, or nearly 189% above the original valuation.That growth does not mean Alpine has generated an equivalent amount in cash or profit. A team valuation estimates what the business could be worth in a transaction. It differs from annual revenue, operating profit and the money available to its owners.The $2.6 billion figure is also an industry estimate, not a confirmed sale price. A completed transaction would provide stronger evidence of what buyers are willing to pay.Still, the change illustrates how investors have reassessed the value of Formula 1 teams as the sport's commercial reach expands.Why Formula 1 team values are climbingFormula 1 offers investors access to a global audience, international sponsorships, hospitality revenue and valuable media partnerships. Teams can also benefit when brands seek to connect with fans through a sport that combines technology, competition and entertainment.The United States has become an important market for the championship. Races in Miami, Austin and Las Vegas have helped increase its visibility among American audiences, while digital content has introduced the sport to fans who might not regularly watch traditional motorsport.That wider appeal can make teams more attractive to sponsors and investors. However, a larger audience does not automatically guarantee higher profits. Racing teams face major operating costs, and results on the track can influence sponsorship opportunities, prize money and public interest.Alpine's position makes its valuation particularly interesting. The team has faced sporting challenges, including a difficult 2025 season, when it finished last in the constructors' championship. Its estimated value has nevertheless continued to attract attention from potential investors.This contrast shows why team values do not always move in step with race results. Investors may also consider future commercial opportunities, the strength of the Formula 1 business model and the possibility of improving a team's performance.For Alpine, the challenge is to turn its commercial potential into stronger results and a more competitive operation. If the team can improve on the track while attracting new sponsors, it could strengthen the case behind its valuation.What Alpine's rising value could mean for MahomesAlpine's valuation growth puts Mahomes' investment in a different light. The quarterback has already established himself as one of the NFL's biggest stars, and his involvement in Formula 1 gives him exposure to another major sports business.The potential financial benefit depends on the size of his individual holding, the terms of the investment and whether the group eventually sells its stake. Those details have not been publicly confirmed, so calculating Mahomes' personal profit from the team's rising value would be speculative.The wider investor group has also attracted interest from potential buyers. In 2026, reports described discussions over a possible sale of its 24% holding, although negotiations with Mercedes did not produce an agreement. That process underlines the difference between a rising estimated value and money an investor can actually realise.For Mahomes, the investment represents a long-term business opportunity rather than an extension of his NFL career. His playing success gives him a public profile, but the value of an investment ultimately depends on commercial performance, ownership terms and the price a buyer is willing to pay.Alpine's estimated rise from $900 million to $2.6 billion is a striking example of the money flowing into Formula 1. Whether that growth ultimately delivers a substantial return for Mahomes remains uncertain. What is clear is that his interests now extend well beyond American football, into a global sport where team ownership has become an increasingly attractive business proposition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Steelers vs. Saints score, live updates: Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh face New Orleans in NFL's first regular-season game in Paris
articles.summary: The Steelers and Saints will play in the league's first-ever regular-season game in Paris.
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will face off in the league's first regular-season game in Paris on Sunday, with kickoff set for 9:30 a.m. ET at the Stade de France.The Steelers (4-2) are riding high after a 13-point fourth-quarter comeback win in overtime over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Aaron Rodgers continues to build on his connection with second-round rookie wideout Germie Bernard, who had 11 catches for 87 yards and a score in Week 6. Running back Jaylen Warren has also been a steady force, averaging 5.5 yards per carry and a career-best 119.7 scrimmage yards per game.The Saints (2-4) snapped a three-game losing streak in Week 6 with a 34-27 win over the New York Giants. Quarterback Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and added another on the ground, and is currently fantasy football's overall QB5 on the year. Despite their slow start to the season, the Saints remain just 1.5 games back of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints head to France in Week 7, airing on NFL Network.

articles.summary: Follow along with all of Sunday's action in Week 7.
articles.body: We've got another loaded NFL Sunday slate on deck in Week 7, following up the morning's Pittsburgh Steelers-New Orleans Saints showdown in Paris with seven games in the early window and three in the afternoon.There are plenty of injuries we're monitoring ahead of the Week 7 kickoff, so be sure to follow along throughout the morning as we keep you up to date on who's in and out.Among the most notable players listed as questionable in Week 7 are Jets RB Breece Hall (groin), Rams WR Puka Nacua (calf) and Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring).The Ravens have ruled out starting quarterback Lamar Jackson for the third straight game with an ankle injury.
